title: Emotional triggers
src: Jung, A Review of the Complex Theory
idea: Jung found that some topics carry a charge far larger than the moment deserves. An outsized reaction points to something unresolved.
apply: When you overreact, write down the trigger, the feeling, and the earliest time you remember feeling it.
remind: An outsized reaction points to something older.
who: Rory, who explodes whenever he is corrected.

msgs.x: Small fix: the date is wrong on slide 3.
Why does everyone assume I am careless?

scenes.nar: A colleague mentions a wrong date on slide three. Rory feels his face heat up and answers sharply.
The event is a typo, but the reaction is enormous. That gap is the clue.

items.x: First memory: a teacher who mocked his mistakes

scenes.nar: Jung called these charged clusters complexes. Rory notes the trigger, the feeling, and the earliest memory of it: a teacher who mocked his mistakes.
Next time he feels the heat rise and names it: old pattern. He replies, thanks, fixing it now, and the moment passes.
